'''Sonia Antoranz Contera''' (born 1970) is a Spanish physicist. She serves as Professor of Biological Physics at the [[University of Oxford]],<ref name="Sonia Contera">{{Cite web|url=https://www.weforum.org/people/sonia-contera/|title=Sonia Contera|website=World Economic Forum|access-date=2019-05-23}}</ref> a senior fellow at the [[Oxford Martin School]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.oxfordmartin.ox.ac.uk/about/people/fellows/|title=Fellows|website=Oxford Martin School|language=en|access-date=2019-05-23}}</ref> and a senior research fellow at [[Green Templeton College, Oxford|Green Templeton College]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.gtc.ox.ac.uk/about/fellows/sonia-antoranz-contera/|title=Dr Sonia Antoranz Contera|website=Green Templeton College|language=en-GB|access-date=2019-05-23}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Sonia Antoranz Contera, born 1970, is from [[Madrid]], Spain.<ref name=":1">{{cite news|url=https://elpais.com/sociedad/2012/12/25/actualidad/1356448155_314831.html|title=La medicina del futuro|last1=Oppenheimer|first1=Walter|date=26 December 2012|work=El País|accessdate=24 May 2019|language=es}}</ref> She studied for her [[Licenciatura]] in physics at the [[Autonomous University of Madrid]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://orcid.org/0000-0002-2371-1206|title=ORCID|website=orcid.org|access-date=2019-05-23}}</ref> She went on to study in Moscow, Prague and Beijing.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://elpais.com/sociedad/2012/12/25/actualidad/1356448155_314831.html|title=La medicina del futuro|last=Oppenheimer|first=Walter|date=2012-12-26|work=El País|access-date=2019-05-23|language=es|issn=1134-6582}}</ref> She received her PhD from [[Osaka University]] in 2000, where her supervisor was [[Hiroshi Iwasaki (biologist)|Hiroshi Iwasaki]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www2.physics.ox.ac.uk/contacts/people/antoranzcontera|title=Sonia Antoranz Contera {{!}} University of Oxford Department of Physics|website=www2.physics.ox.ac.uk|access-date=2019-05-23}}</ref><ref name=":0" />

Having traveled extensively during her education, Contera speaks Spanish, English, Chinese, Czech, Russian, Danish, Japanese, German and French.<ref name=":1" />

== Research and career ==
Contera's research uses physics and nanotechnology to understand biological problems.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://epsrc.ukri.org/about/people/soniacontera/|title=Sonia Contera - EPSRC website|website=epsrc.ukri.org|access-date=2019-05-23}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.science.org/content/article/biosystems-nanotechnology-big-opportunities-science-small|title=Biosystems nanotechnology: Big opportunities in the science of the small|last=Levine|first=Alaina G.|date=November 14, 2014|website=Science|publisher=AAAS|language=en|access-date=2019-05-25}}</ref> She has a special interest in the role of mechanics in biology and designs nanomaterials that mimic biological functions for biomedical applications such as drug delivery<ref name="Sonia Contera"/> and tissue engineering.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.elmundo.es/elmundo/2011/08/22/nanotecnologia/1314000681.html|title=Nano-ingeniería de tejidos para medicina regenerativa|last=Luna|first=Mónica|date=August 22, 2011|website=El Mundo|language=es|access-date=2019-05-25}}</ref> In 2003, she began working at Oxford.<ref name=":1" /> Contera was Co-Director of the Oxford Martin Programme on Nanotechnology for Medicine from 2008 to 2013.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.oxfordmartin.ox.ac.uk/people/29|title=Professor Sonia Contera {{!}} People|website=Oxford Martin School|language=en|access-date=2019-05-23}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.lavanguardia.com/vida/20160506/401603320193/estereotipos-espanoles-expatriados.html|title=¿Somos como dicen los estereotipos?|last=Rius|first=Mayte|date=2016-05-07|website=La Vanguardia|access-date=2019-05-25}}</ref> In 2014–2016, she was a Member of the [[World Economic Forum]] Global Agenda Council on Nanotechnology.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://widgets.weforum.org/global-agenda-councils-interactive-2014/|title=Global Agenda Councils - World Economic Forum|website=widgets.weforum.org|language=en-US|access-date=2019-05-23}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.elmundo.es/papel/lideres/2016/07/19/578df93722601d74738b4600.html|title=Sonia es profesora en Oxford: "Eliminaría los exámenes en primaria"|last=Paniagua|first=Esther|date=2016-07-19|website=El Mundo|language=es|access-date=2019-05-25}}</ref> In 2017, Contera was appointed Chair of the [[Scanning probe microscopy|Scanning Probe Microscopy]] Section of the [[Royal Microscopical Society]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.rms.org.uk/network-collaborate/science-sections/scanning-probe-microscopy.html|title=Scanning Probe Microscopy|website=www.rms.org.uk|access-date=2019-05-24}}</ref>

Contera's book ''Nano Comes to Life: How Nanotechnology is transforming medicine and the future of Biology (Princeton University Press)'' was published December 2019.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.waterstones.com/book/nano-comes-to-life/sonia-contera//9780691168807|title=Nano Comes to Life by Sonia Contera {{!}} Waterstones|website=www.waterstones.com|language=en|access-date=2019-05-23}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|title=NANO COMES TO LIFE : how nanotechnology is transforming medicine and the future of biology.|last=CONTERA, SONIA.|date=2019|publisher=PRINCETON UNIV PRESS|isbn=978-0691168807|location=[S.l.]|oclc=1099683369}}</ref> The book was reviewed by Nature,<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Kiser|first=Barbara|date=2019-12-10|title=A heliocentric epic, volcanic viniculture, and cartoon chemistry: Books in brief|journal=Nature|language=en|volume=576|issue=7786|pages=207|doi=10.1038/d41586-019-03757-0|doi-access=free}}</ref> Nature Physics,<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Horejs|first=Christine-Maria|date=March 2020|title=I, nanorobot|journal=Nature Physics|language=en|volume=16|issue=3|pages=239|doi=10.1038/s41567-020-0820-1|issn=1745-2481|doi-access=free}}</ref> the New Scientist,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Educational access digital subscriptions {{!}} New Scientist|url=https://institutions.newscientist.com/article/mg24432580-300-dont-miss-knotty-sculptures-deadly-diseases-and-molecular-machines/|access-date=2021-09-15|website=institutions.newscientist.com}}</ref> BBC Science Focus<ref>{{Cite web|title=Sonia Contera on nanotechnology|url=https://www.sciencefocus.com/future-technology/sonia-contera-on-nanotechnology/|access-date=2021-09-15|website=BBC Science Focus Magazine|language=en}}</ref> and was featured in BBC Radio 4 "Start of the Week".<ref>{{Cite web|title=BBC Radio 4 - Start the Week, Numbers, nightmares and nanotech|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/m000c9lj|access-date=2021-09-15|website=BBC|language=en-GB}}</ref> It was published in paperback in 2022, in Chinese by CITIC press and in Japanese by Newton Press.

Contera is also a public speaker on the medical, philosophical and social consequences of  the science emerging at the interface of nanotechnology, physics and biology; she has spoken in forums such as the Royal Institution of Great Britain<ref>{{Citation|title=The Issues We Face at the Nano Scale - with Sonia Contera|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bEjx48z8Lzs|language=en|access-date=2021-09-15}}</ref> She also writes on communication and the mission of science.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Contera|first=Sonia|date=May 2021|title=Communication is central to the mission of science|journal=Nature Reviews Materials|language=en|volume=6|issue=5|pages=377–378|doi=10.1038/s41578-021-00316-w|pmid=33868716 |issn=2058-8437|pmc=8043085}}</ref>
